tagline: A road to Preston’s old center, where farms supplied a river port.
intro: Route 164’s designated scenic section connects the Griswold town line with the center of Preston City. It is called Jewett City Road on this stretch, with a Route 165 junction in the village. The historic village district includes Georgian, Federal, and Greek Revival buildings, with houses built by farmers and merchants during Preston’s trading years.

Preston City was established as a town center in 1686 and became a focus for sending farm goods to Norwich. From that Thames River port, local produce traveled to other East Coast ports. The direct road between Preston City and Jewett City became Route 164 in the 1932 renumbering, with no major alignment or designation changes since.

Traveling south from the Griswold line, Jewett City Road reaches the village and Route 165 at the scenic section’s end. Old Shetucket and Amos Roads were major thoroughfares before the 1930s; they now lie within the historic district. Beyond the village, Route 164 continues south as Preston Plains Road toward Route 2.

moments.title: Timothy Lester Farmstead
moments.text: Stone walls line the surviving 43 acres of the Timothy Lester Farmstead, where the landscape is gradually returning to woodland. At Crary and Browning Roads in southern Griswold, the farmhouse was built in stages beginning circa 1741. The house served as a garrison and training ground during the American Revolutionary War. The Lester children signed petitions for Griswold’s separation from Preston, which took place in 1815. Sold outside the family in 1857, the farm remained in agricultural use until the middle of the twentieth century. Beside the central-chimney farmhouse stand an eighteenth-century barn and a small wellhouse.

moments.title: Preston City Baptist Church
moments.text: The church’s steeple came twenty years after the building. Built in 1812, the Preston City Baptist Church was turned to face a different direction and received its three-stage steeple and bell tower in 1832. A pyramidal roof tops the tower. It is one of the wood-frame buildings contributing to the village’s historic district.
moments.notice: The steeple rises in three stages to a pyramidal roof.

moments.title: Old Town Pound
moments.text: A stone-walled enclosure on Amos Road is Preston City’s Old Town Pound. It served as a pound, a common feature of British medieval villages where stray livestock might be held. Amos Road itself was a major thoroughfare before the 1930s, and the enclosure contributes to the Preston City Historic District.
